title: Information and voting: Evidence from Peru's 2026 general elections
abstract: arXiv:2606.01687v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Logistical failures during Peru's 2026 general elections postponed voting at thirteen locations in Lima Sur, so that roughly 55,000 registered electors cast ballots after election-night estimates and partial official returns had become public. We exploit this natural experiment to study whether public signals about candidate viability reshape choices on simultaneous presidential and legislative ballots. In our model of joint electoral choice, voters update beliefs about runoff qualification and legislative prospects and trade off candidate affinity, office-specific preferences, and the value of aligned representation. Upward revisions to perceived viability raise a candidate's presidential support and, through aligned representation, that of its legislative list, while office-specific preferences can generate divergent responses across ballots. Using cardinality matching, we compare delayed locations to election-day locations balance

translated_title: 信息与投票：来自秘鲁2026年大选的证据
translated_abstract: 秘鲁2026年大选期间的后勤故障导致利马南部十三个投票点的投票被推迟，使得约5.5万名登记选民在选举夜预估结果和部分官方计票结果公布之后才进行投票。我们利用这一自然实验研究关于候选人胜选可能性的公开信号是否会重塑选民在同时举行的总统选举和立法选举中的选择。在我们的联合选举选择模型中，选民会更新关于候选人能否进入第二轮投票以及其立法前景的信念，并在候选人亲和度、针对特定职位的偏好以及对齐代表的价值之间进行权衡。对候选人胜选可能性的认知上调会提高该候选人的总统选举支持率，并通过代表性对齐效应提高其立法竞选名单的支持率，而针对特定职位的偏好则可能在不同的选票上产生分化的反应。使用基数匹配方法，我们将延迟投票的地点与选举日正常投票的地点进行比较以实现平衡。
tldr: 本文利用秘鲁2026年大选中因后勤故障造成的延迟投票这一自然实验，首次实证研究了公开的选举结果信息如何通过更新选民对候选人胜选可能性的信念，同时影响总统选举和立法选举中的投票行为。
en_tdlr: Exploiting delayed voting caused by logistical failures in Peru's 2026 general elections as a natural experiment, this paper provides novel evidence that public signals about candidate viability reshape simultaneous presidential and legislative voting by updating voters' beliefs.
